extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners; patent practitioners and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Official Korean Intellectual Property Office examination guidelines for evaluating patent applications under the Korean Patent Act, covering patentability (industrial applicability, novelty, inventive step), unpatentable subject matter, inventive step analysis, software/AI inventions, and procedural practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Article 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per Article 29 (Industrial applicability, novelty, inventive step): An invention shall be industrially applicable; must not be publicly known/used domestically or in writing/electronic media before filing; must involve an inventive step over the publicly known art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three elements (industrial applicability, novelty, inventive step) are the core statutory tests examiners apply when determining patentability under the Korean Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpatentable inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Per Korean Patent Act: inventions contrary to public order, morality, or public health; methods of treatment of the human body (similar to EPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should reject subject matter that conflicts with public order/morality/public health and be aware that methods of treatment of the human body are considered unpatentable under KIPO practice, analogous to EPO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step analysis (four-step test)
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO uses a test similar to other jurisdictions: 1) Determine the closest cited art; 2) Identify differences; 3) Examine whether differences could be easily made by combining cited prior art; 4) Consider effects achieved by the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these sequential steps to assess whether the claimed differences over the closest prior art would have been obvious to a person skilled in the art, taking into account the technical effects produced by the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer/software invention eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO accepts software-related inventions if: the invention is a 'creation of a technical idea using laws of nature'; software performs a technical processing; information processing is concretely realized using hardware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be allowable, software claims must be framed to show a technical solution (not mere abstract algorithms), demonstrate technical processing, and link the information-processing steps to concrete hardware realization or technical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI / Fourth Industrial Revolution technology guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO announced Patent Examination Guidelines for key technology areas related to the Fourth Industrial Revolution, including machine learning based artificial intelligence, on January 18, 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are specialized examination guidelines and examples addressing AI/ML and related emerging technologies; examiners and applicants should consult these sector-specific provisions when evaluating AI-related claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: International harmonization and use of IP5-derived standards/examples
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO established 39 examination standards based on a comparative study of the IP5 offices (Korea, US, Europe, Japan, China) and increased the number of application examples to 50 to help examiners better understand the standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are expected to apply harmonized standards informed by IP5 practice and use the expanded set of concrete application examples to promote consistent examination. Applicants can use those examples to understand claim drafting and prosecution expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and procedural practice expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Process considerations: Korean prosecution typically is faster than US/EPO (12-18 months to first action); there are strict written argument requirements; limited examiner interview practice; appeals to the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board (IPTAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and practitioners should prepare comprehensive written arguments (given the limited interview practice), anticipate a relatively fast first-action timeframe, and be prepared to appeal to IPTAB if necessary. Examiners follow these procedural norms in handling cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline scope and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines cover: General Rules including Capacity; Article 36 Patent Act of Korea; Application Requirements; Examination Methods; Instructions on Examination; Unpatentable Inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document is organized to guide examiners through statutory provisions, application formalities, substantive examination methods, specific instructions for examination practice, and lists of unpatentable subject matter; users should consult the relevant section for detailed criteria and examples.
